sections.title: Start with what you want to repeat
paragraphs: A good typing site makes the activity you need easy to repeat. If you want to work through a word list, change the duration, or practice specific text, Monkeytype puts those choices beside the typing area. Its time, words, quote, zen and custom controls were visible in our review. You can change the task without turning it into a competition.

TypeRacer puts the race first, but it also has a Practice Yourself option. We opened that option as a guest and reached a single-player quote with a typing field. You do not have to join a public race every time you want to use it. Choose the social setting when opponents motivate you; choose practice when you want fewer variables.

sections.title: A different WPM does not identify the better tool
paragraphs: A short familiar word list and a passage with capitals and punctuation are different tests. Before comparing scores, match the text style and test length as closely as possible. Monkeytype has quote mode, so comparing its default word list against a TypeRacer passage is an avoidable mismatch.

Correction rules and timing also affect the result. We do not publish a fixed conversion such as “subtract 10 WPM”: this review did not run a controlled benchmark. Keep a baseline within one mode, then use another site as a different exercise rather than a replacement measuring instrument.

sections.title: What the screens actually let you do
paragraphs: Monkeytype’s quote control exposes length choices, including short and long. That makes it a sensible place to vary reading and punctuation difficulty while keeping the familiar test interface. The screenshot shows that quote mode exists; it is not restricted to random words.

TypeRacer’s home screen separates Enter a Typing Race, Practice Yourself and Create Racetrack. Its guest message says an account saves races and gives access to detailed stats. Some curated-text selectors were disabled in our guest view, so do not assume every text option is available under the same access conditions.

sections.title: When staying with your current site makes sense
paragraphs: Stay with Monkeytype if its solo controls already support your routine. Stay with TypeRacer if your friends already use its tracks or racing helps you return consistently. There is no evidence in this review that changing sites alone improves typing ability. A repeatable practice habit is a better reason to choose than a flattering single score.

sections.title: Want practice and small friend races together?
paragraphs: Monkeytype Racer, the site publishing this article, offers solo practice and private rooms for two to five total racers. Everyone in a room receives the same quote and shared start; mistakes must be corrected to finish. It is an option for that combined workflow, not an official Monkeytype or TypeRacer mode.

Our five-racer limit is a real constraint. We are not recommending our product as a substitute for every established competition, community or advanced practice setting. If your current tool fits, keep it; try a friend room when the group experience is what you are missing.

sections.title: Who decides the next exercise?
paragraphs: The useful difference is how the next session gets chosen. Monkeytype lets you specify the format: a timed test, a word count, a quote, an open-ended zen session or custom text. That fits someone who already knows what to practice and wants to repeat it under similar conditions.

Keybr makes individual keys part of the lesson. Its official help describes generating words from a limited letter set, increasing the frequency of a target key and adding letters as you progress. The practice screen shows that structure directly through the current-key indicator and active or locked letters.

sections.title: What Keybr’s indicators mean
paragraphs: Our fresh Keybr session showed an uncalibrated current key that needed more samples, alongside speed, accuracy and a daily goal. That is a useful reminder to let an exercise gather evidence before treating a single result as a verdict on your ability.

The help page explains that a target letter appears more frequently and that previously practiced letters can weaken when new ones are introduced. Follow those indicators when choosing what to repeat. We inspected the interface and documentation; we did not complete the full progression or measure a training effect.

sections.title: Where Monkeytype gives you more direct choice
paragraphs: If you want to practice a particular passage, change duration or switch from familiar words to punctuation-heavy prose, Monkeytype puts test controls beside the text. Its quote mode includes length choices. You do not need to change products simply to move beyond random words.

This choice also means taking responsibility for the exercise. Repeating only your most comfortable settings may yield satisfying scores without addressing a difficult letter or text style. Pick settings based on the task you want to improve, and keep them consistent when tracking progress.

sections.title: A simple way to use both
paragraphs: Try a short Keybr session focused on its current target, then a Monkeytype quote exercise. Treat the first as focused repetition and the second as an opportunity to use those letters in prose. This is a suggested routine, not a tested prescription or a promise of faster learning.

Keep separate baselines. Keybr’s constrained letter set and a full quote are different tasks, so their WPM numbers need not match. Record accuracy and recurring mistakes as well as speed. Do not move on solely because another site produces a higher number.

sections.title: Choose by the help you need
paragraphs: Keep Monkeytype if you already have a productive custom practice routine. Try Keybr if you want the software to make individual keys harder to ignore. Its navigation also includes Multiplayer and Typing Test; this comparison focuses on its practice lessons, not a claim that it has no other modes.
Neither product needs to replace the other. Choose one primary place to track progress, and use the second for an exercise your routine is missing.

sections.title: Both products let you practice alone
paragraphs: We opened TypeRacer’s Practice Yourself option as a guest and reached a quote with a typing field. Its home screen also explains that an account saves races and gives access to detailed stats. Some curated-text controls were disabled in our guest view.

Our separate practice page defaults to quotes and exposes timed, word-count, zen and custom modes. The quote and one-minute landing pages are directly playable. Our accuracy guide includes custom drills, and an imperfect practice result can offer another run focused on attempted words you missed.

sections.title: Compare the workflow, not an assumed speed advantage
paragraphs: A useful small-group trial is to create a room, invite a friend, complete a race and start a rematch. Decide whether that sequence is easy enough for the people who will join. Our private-room flow is covered by browser tests; the competitor inspection here did not include a completed private event.

Do not expect identical WPM across products or text types. We do not claim better latency, stronger anti-cheat or faster learning from this comparison. The reason to choose our site is the particular combination of guest races and nearby practice.

sections.title: When TypeRacer remains the sensible choice
paragraphs: If your group already enjoys TypeRacer and its track setup works, there is no need to move for the sake of moving. Try Monkeytype Racer when a small room, direct practice and rematches address something you want to change. We publish this article, and our product is independent of TypeRacer.

verdict: Choose Monkeytype for a solo routine built around its test controls. Choose Monkeytype Racer when you want small friend races alongside practice. Similar-looking mode names do not imply identical settings, saved history or complete feature parity.

sections.title: The homepage tells you what each product is for
paragraphs: Monkeytype opens into its typing-test experience. Time, words, quote, zen and custom controls let you shape the exercise directly. For someone who already knows which test to repeat, that is a useful place to start.

Monkeytype Racer starts with racing. You can type the homepage quote as a warmup without entering the public queue; only the primary race button joins it. Solo practice lives at a separate route and defaults to quotes. This structure keeps the decision to compete explicit.

sections.title: Shared mode names are only the beginning
paragraphs: Both inspected practice interfaces expose time, words, quote, zen and custom modes. Monkeytype’s quote control includes length choices, so prose practice is already available there. You do not need our site simply because you want capitals and punctuation in a passage.

The presence of the same mode names does not establish full parity. If you rely on a specific language, advanced setting or saved-history workflow, check it in our product before switching. We do not promise to reproduce every Monkeytype setting or transfer its account data.

sections.title: Where our friend rooms change the activity
paragraphs: Our private rooms hold two to five total racers, including the host. Guests can join through a shared link, ready up and start together. Every participant receives the same quote, and errors must be corrected to finish. The host can open a rematch for another round.

We did not find a friend-room control on Monkeytype’s reviewed test screen. That is the scope of our observation, not an exhaustive claim about every extension, community tool or future feature. Use our rooms when a shared live session is the missing activity.

sections.title: Keep practice useful between races
paragraphs: Our quote and one-minute pages launch directly into the promised exercise. The accuracy guide offers deterministic custom drills, and missed-word practice can focus a subsequent run on mistakes from the previous attempt. These are options for a short practice session between group rounds.

Monkeytype’s custom mode remains a sensible choice if you already prepare your own exercises. Do not abandon a productive routine just to consolidate websites. You can keep your solo baseline there and use our rooms when friends want a race.

sections.title: Choose without confusing the brands or scores
paragraphs: Monkeytype Racer is independent of Monkeytype. Accounts and saved results should be treated as separate, and we make no promise of complete feature parity. Our recommendation is based on the activity each product offers, not on an official relationship.

Compare results only within reasonably consistent text and timing conditions. If you alternate between a solo word test and a shared quote race, keep separate baselines. Choose Monkeytype when its solo setup is the reason you practice; choose our product when small-group racing is what you want to add.
